jobs.title: Adjunct CNC Machining & Programming Instructor Workforce & Skills Training
jobs.description: Position Summary Adjunct Instructor positions are temporary, part-time positions hired on an as-needed basis to support workforce and skills training initiatives. The Adjunct CNC Machining & Programming Instructor will create a hands-on learning environment that supports adult learners in developing practical machining, CNC operation, setup, programming, and troubleshooting skills aligned with modern manufacturing needs. This role focuses on delivering non-credit CNC machining and programming training for workforce development. Training may range from introductory machining and CNC operation to advanced setup and programming based on instructor expertise and employer needs. Instructors may teach at Ivy Tech Community College - Richmond or onsite at employer locations throughout the surrounding service area. Applicants are not required to have expertise in every CNC machine, controller, or programming platform. Instructors may be selected to teach courses within their specific area(s) of professional expertise. Major Responsibilities Deliver high-quality, hands-on CNC machining and programming training in classroom, lab, and employer-site settings. • Facilitate adult learning through machine demonstrations, setup exercises, programming activities, troubleshooting scenarios, and practical applications. • Provide or assist with course outlines, instructional materials, lab activities, and assessments aligned with workforce training objectives. • Demonstrate safe and proper operation of CNC machines, tooling, workholding devices, and related equipment. • Adapt instruction to participants with varying levels of machining and manufacturing experience. • Maintain accurate attendance, progress, assessment, and course-completion records. • Submit required course documentation within established timelines. • Support participants with technical questions and skill development throughout training. • Address participant concerns and collaborate with Ivy Tech Workforce/Skills Training staff as needed. • Meet all scheduled training sessions as assigned. • Utilize instructional technologies such as PowerPoint, Canvas, CNC simulation software, CAD/CAM software, or manufacturer-specific programming platforms when appropriate. • Promote a professional, respectful, inclusive, and safety-focused learning environment. • Ensure the safe use of machines, tooling, measuring equipment, and laboratory resources CNC Machining & Programming Training Areas Qualified instructors may teach in one or more of the following areas based on their experience and expertise: • CNC Machining Fundamentals • CNC Machine Operation • CNC Mill Setup and Operation • CNC Lathe Setup and Operation • CNC Programming • G-Code and M-Code Programming • Conversational Programming • CNC Setup, Tooling, and Workholding • Machine Offsets and Tool Compensation • Blueprint Reading • Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T;) • Precision Measurement and Inspection • Machining Math • Cutting Tools, Speeds, and Feeds • Manual Machining Fundamentals • CNC Troubleshooting • Process Improvement and Cycle-Time Optimization • CAD/CAM Programming • Mastercam or other CAM software • FANUC CNC Controls • Haas CNC Controls • Other CNC machining, programming, and advanced manufacturing topics based on employer needs Instructors may also assist in developing or customizing short-term CNC training for employer partners based on specific machines, controllers, software, manufacturing processes, or workforce skill gaps Minimum Qualifications • Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant hands-on CNC machining, CNC programming, tool and die, manufacturing, or related technical experience. • Demonstrated expertise in at least one CNC machining or programming discipline. • Working knowledge of CNC machine operation, setup, tooling, machining processes, and applicable safety practices. • Ability to explain technical machining concepts clearly and translate industry experience into practical, hands-on instruction

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty - Non Credit Skills Training
jobs.description: GENERAL PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THE POSITION: Adjunct faculty work with the Employer Consultant and Program Manager to consult, develop and deliver short-term off the shelf or customized programs to meet the in-demand real-time needs of employers and community stakeholders in our service area. Skills Training (non-credit) programs are short term commitments and may include delivery on campus, at an employer location or a community facility in any of our five service area counties (Wayne, Rush, Fayette, Union and Randolph). Adjuncts are compensated based on a variety of factors related to required skill sets, required certifications if applicable and experience. MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES: Instructional delivery or facilitation that meet learning objectives established in contracted or open enrollment projects as assigned / accepted. Some projects may include employer consultation in order for the Employer Consultant to create a proposal and cost. Many courses are developed, or can be tweaked to meet needs identified, other times programs need to be developed or customized. The College can provide access to many resources – curriculums and past projects for reference as well as other faculty or locations who may have experience to assist. Adjuncts will be responsible for appropriate use of College labs and equipment that may be used in the course of delivery. Adjuncts will provide all materials developed for a course delivery to the EC/Program Manager upon completion and will ensure documentation of student attendance and pass/fail/grade per project is completed. QUALIFICATIONS : Qualifications vary project to project and are related to the subject matter being taught or facilitated and client desired outcomes. Ideal candidates have experiential knowledge in the subject area, experience with adult instruction or training / facilitation, good listening skills, dynamic communication skills, computer skills that allow interface with basic systems and in-class IT equipment (training provided) and present themselves – and the College – in a professional manner. Confidentiality of client material and projects is required at all times. Projects may be in a variety of areas – safety, supervision, computers, maintenance topics, manufacturing, quality, lean, etc. All persons interested in working on any type of short term high quality training project we may encounter should apply to be considered for projects as they develop. jobs.description: Ivy Tech Madison is currently accepting applications for an Adult Basic Education Instructor located at the Wabash Valley Correctional Facility in Carlisle, IN. Come join our team and help our students achieve their GED! General Purpose / Position Summary: The IDOC Licensed Teacher provides high-quality instruction to incarcerated adult learners in Ivy Tech Correctional Education programs. The teacher delivers curriculum-aligned lessons, assesses student progress, maintains required documentation, and collaborates with site leadership to support successful program outcomes and re-entry preparation. This is a full-time, year-round teaching position located at the Wabash Valley Correctional Facility. Major Job Responsibilities: Instruction • Provide high-quality, standard-aligned instruction. • Design and deliver lessons that promote active learning. • Begin and end classes on time per facility and Ivy Tech schedules. • Present clear explanations to ensure student understanding. • Check for understanding throughout instruction. • Integrate technology and approved resources when available. • Support diverse learning needs, including IEP/504/ELL. • Encourage student engagement and participation. • Support distance-learning and supplemental platforms. Learning Assessment & Academic Progress • Assess student learning using formal and informal tools. • Evaluate student performance fairly and consistently. • Provide timely, constructive feedback. • Administer TABE, GED Ready, and other assessments. • Maintain accurate student grades and records. Documentation & Compliance • Maintain accurate attendance and documentation. • Ensure accurate entry into InTERS/Delta as required. • Submit completion documentation promptly. • Maintain student files per policy requirements. • Support FERPA, security, and compliance requirements. • Support continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes and instructional audits. • Care for classroom materials and technology. Program & Operational Support • Collaborate with Site Manager and instructional team. • Participate in meetings, training, and coaching. • Support student onboarding, placement, and orientation. • Assist with classroom and testing preparation. • Support events such as graduations and recognition. Classroom Culture & Student Support • Build positive rapport while maintaining boundaries. • Model professional and prosocial behaviors. • Promote safe, inclusive classroom culture. • Provide academic advising and re-entry guidance. Indiana Tech enrolls nearly 1,500 students in its traditional undergraduate programs on its picturesque main campus, and nearly 5,000 students in its adult and online program. We offer degrees at the associate, bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral levels and undergraduate and graduate certificates. Over 41% of our students are either globally or domestically diverse; this contributes to our unique vibrant and inclusive campus community. All academic programs are designed to provide students with relevant and practical experiences, including an emphasis on internships. The university is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. Indiana Tech is committed to fostering a welcoming and respectful environment for all. We actively support the recruitment, engagement, and retention of students, faculty, and staff from a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We believe that creating a sense of connection and support across our campus community plays an essential role in preparing students to succeed and contribute in a global society. Indiana Tech has big plans for its future. Learn more at Indiana Tech Strategic Plan or strategicplan.indianatech.edu . Indiana Tech is seeking an innovative, collaborative, and faculty-centered leader to serve as its AI Faculty Strategist. Reporting to the Executive Director of the AI Institute, with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President for Academic Affairs, this position serves as the university’s primary faculty consultant for artificial intelligence pedagogy and instructional innovation. The AI Faculty Strategist leads Indiana Tech’s faculty-facing initiative for teaching AI within the curriculum and helps faculty build the knowledge, confidence, and instructional judgment needed to effectively integrate AI into teaching and learning. Serving concurrently as Director of the Teaching Excellence Center, the AI Faculty Strategist plays a central role in advancing Indiana Tech’s institutional AI strategy by helping faculty navigate the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence in higher education. This position works closely with the Warrior AI Readiness Manager, the Director of Curriculum Design & AI Integration, academic deans, instructional designers, and faculty across disciplines to move instructors from AI awareness to meaningful course and program transformation. The AI Faculty Strategist serves as the primary point of contact for faculty seeking guidance on AI pedagogy, instructional design, assessment redesign, and responsible AI integration. The successful candidate will provide individual consultation, facilitate professional development opportunities, mentor faculty participating in AI innovation initiatives, and help faculty identify opportunities for course redesign and instructional improvement. Faculty projects selected for full redesign and implementation will be carried out in partnership with the Curriculum Design team. Additional responsibilities include developing and facilitating workshops, seminars, communities of practice, and faculty-development programs focused on AI in higher education. The Strategist will use institutional readiness data to identify coaching opportunities, contribute faculty-focused programming to university-wide AI initiatives, create instructional resources and teaching guides, support grant-related activities, and represent Indiana Tech’s AI efforts at institutional, regional, and national conferences. jobs.description: Position Title: Assistant / Associate / Professor of Elementary Education Compensation: $70,000 - $95,000 Department: Elementary Education Start Date: 08/02/2027 About this opportunity: Ball State University’s Department of Elementary Education invites applications for a full-time, tenure-line faculty position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank beginning August 2027. While candidates at all ranks will be considered, we are particularly interested in applicants whose experiences and accomplishments support appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level. Salary range for Assistant Professor: $70,000 - $75,000 Salary range for Associate Professor or Professor: $75,000 - $95,000 We seek a collaborative teacher-scholar committed to preparing highly effective elementary educators and advancing knowledge in teaching and learning. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate programs in elementary education, with particular emphasis on literacy, inclusive teaching practices, and curriculum and instruction. We are especially interested in candidates whose teaching, scholarship, and professional engagement reflect current research and evidence-based practices in elementary education and who can contribute leadership to the department’s teaching, research, partnerships, and program development. This position offers opportunities to teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, supervise candidates in field-based settings, maintain a productive program of research and scholarship, collaborate with faculty and school/community partners, and contribute to the ongoing development of innovative educator preparation programs. Candidates at the Associate or Full Professor level should demonstrate a sustained record of scholarly productivity and professional contributions appropriate to rank. Employer will consider sponsorship. What you'll do and what you will bring: Duties and responsibilities : Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary education, with particular emphasis on literacy, inclusive teaching practices, and curriculum and instruction; supervise practicum and other field-based experiences; establish and maintain an active program of research and scholarly publication; pursue opportunities for external funding as appropriate; engage in partnerships with schools, families, communities, and other educational organizations; advise and mentor graduate students, including doctoral students; collaborate with faculty on program development and improvement; provide leadership appropriate to experience and rank; and provide professional university, college, and departmental service. Salary range for Assistant Professor: $70,000 - $75,000 Salary range for Associate Professor or Professor: $75,000 - $95,000 Minimum Qualifications: Earned doctorate in Elementary Education, Literacy, Curriculum and Instruction, or closely related field from an accredited institution by the date of appointment. At least three years (6 academic semesters/24 months) of teaching experience in an elementary (K-6) setting Demonstrated record of scholarly productivity, as evidenced by refereed presentations at regional, national, or international conferences and/or scholarly publications such as refereed journal articles, book chapters, or books. For appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level, a record of teaching, scholarship, and service commensurate with expectations for the respective rank. Preferred Qualifications: University-level teaching experience (at least one academic semester/3 months). Expertise literacy instruction and knowledge of current research and evidence-based approaches to literacy teaching, including developments associated with the Science of Reading. jobs.description: Assistant/Associate Professor of Physical Therapy Assistant/Associate Professor of Physical Therapy Fort Wayne, Indiana Summary The Trine University Doctor of Physical Therapy program in Fort Wayne, IN, seeks an individual with expertise in teaching graduate physical therapy students. Depending on individual qualifications, opportunities exist to teach foundational topics of physical therapy practice or specific practice areas such as integumentary care, orthopedics, or cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. jobs.description: Employment Opportunity Detail Assistant Athletic Trainer / Instructor of Athletic Training The University of Evansville Department of Athletics is seeking a dedicated, student-centered, and collaborative athletic training professional to join our Sports Medicine team. This position will assist the Associate Athletic Director for Sports Medicine in providing comprehensive healthcare services for University student-athletes while also supporting the School of Health Sciences Athletic Training Program through classroom instruction and clinical education. The successful candidate will serve as the primary athletic trainer for Women's Volleyball and may be assigned additional sport coverage as determined by the Associate Athletic Director for Sports Medicine. This position combines clinical athletic training responsibilities with teaching and clinical supervision duties, providing a unique opportunity to contribute to both student-athlete health and athletic training education. Key Responsibilities The Assistant Athletic Trainer / Instructor will balance athletic training services, educational responsibilities, and administrative duties. Primary responsibilities include: Athletic Training & Sports Medicine Provide prevention, evaluation, treatment, and rehabilitation of athletic injuries and illnesses for assigned student-athletes. Develop and implement injury prevention and rehabilitation programs in collaboration with the Sports Medicine team. Deliver healthcare education and counseling to student-athletes. Communicate effectively with student-athletes, physicians, coaching staff, and parents, when appropriate, regarding injury status and treatment plans. Coordinate and provide medical coverage for practices, competitions, and team travel. Collaborate with physicians and allied healthcare professionals to ensure comprehensive care for student-athletes. Maintain accurate electronic medical records and injury documentation. Assist with insurance claim processing and related administrative functions. Support scheduling and coordination of medical coverage for home and away athletic events. Teaching & Clinical Education Provide instruction within the School of Health Sciences Athletic Training Program. Serve as a clinical preceptor and mentor for Athletic Training students. Supervise, educate, and evaluate Athletic Training students and athletic training interns. Assist with recruitment and retention efforts for the Athletic Training Program. Promote professional development and evidence-based practice among students. Administrative Responsibilities Maintain accurate records related to athletic training services, student clinical experiences, and insurance processing. Ensure compliance with University, NCAA, BOC, state licensure, and accreditation requirements. Participate in departmental meetings, professional development activities, and other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Master's degree in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Health Sciences, or a closely related field. Board of Certification (BOC) certification. Indiana Athletic Trainer License or eligibility for licensure. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with student-athletes, students, faculty, coaches, healthcare providers, and parents. Ability to perform the physical requirements of the position, including lifting and carrying equipment and supplies. Ability to work a flexible schedule that includes evenings, weekends, holidays, and team travel. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with softball or similar overhead-throwing sports. The assistant faculty lead will work collaboratively with the faculty lead; educational technology and instructional design team; and campus chairs and the curriculum committee(s) to ensure effective course delivery. In compliance with the College’s Out of State Workers Policy, only candidates who will reside in and work from the states of Indiana, Illinois, Kentucky, Michigan and Ohio will be considered for this position. Work with IvyOnline course schedulers to ensure appropriate courses are scheduled each term. The preferred start date is August 2027; however, an earlier start date may be considered based on candidate availability. Salary will be commensurate with experience and academic credentials. The successful applicant will demonstrate the ability to teach and mentor both entry-level and post-professional OTD students. The Tenure rank faculty position will also be responsible for developing an active research agenda in their area of expertise, generate external funding, engage in online and classroom teaching, and provide school and university service.Duties for the Assistant or Associate Professor Position: 40% Teaching 50% Research 10% Service/Engagement The Occupational Therapy Program ranked by US News & World Report as #1 in the state and 23rd in the nation is part of a dynamic academic and research community that includes four programs in the Department of Graduate Health Professions (Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Nutrition and Dietetics, and Physician Assistant) eight departments in the School of Health and Human Sciences (SHHS), 15 research labs and institutes, and over 400 clinical and community partnerships.IU Indianapolis is a leading urban research university located in downtown Indianapolis, serving more than 25,000 students across a wide range of programs. Through hands-on learning and strong community partnerships, IU Indianapolis prepares students to make a meaningful impact in their careers and in Indiana’s growing economy. jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Nurse Anesthesia Program
jobs.description: Employment Opportunity Detail Assistant Director/Assistant Professor - Nurse Anesthesia Program The University of Evansville invites applications for a motivated, expert clinician-educator to join our esteemed Nurse Anesthesia Program as an Assistant Program Director and Assistant Professor. This position is scheduled to begin on January 1, 2027. In this dynamic leadership and faculty role, you will work closely with the Program Director to oversee daily department operations, guide curriculum development, and assess student outcomes to ensure continuous program excellence. Whether you choose a tenure-track path or focus on instructional and clinical leadership, this position offers a unique balance of academic administration, teaching, mentorship, and optional clinical practice. Key Responsibilities Curriculum Management: Lead curriculum development and assessment for the nurse anesthesia program, utilizing student evaluations and faculty feedback to drive continuous improvement and meet programmatic outcomes. Didactic Instruction & Course Coordination: Develop, organize, deliver, and assess assigned courses. Manage syllabi, schedules, lecture objectives, and evaluation tools while maintaining expert knowledge in subject matter. Student Advising & Mentorship: Mentor professional-phase nurse anesthesia students throughout their course of study, offering academic, professional, and personal guidance. Record Keeping: Maintain accurate course and student records for assessment, submitting all documentation to the University by established deadlines. Recruitment & Community Outreach: Represent the program to prospective students, families, the University, and the broader community. Committee Service: Actively participate in required programmatic committees as well as College and University-wide committees. Scholarly & Professional Engagement: Engage in ongoing scholarship, professional development, and consulting activities, including attendance at conferences and research initiatives. Required Qualifications Education: Must hold a doctoral degree (DNP, DNAP, or PhD) from an accredited institution recognized by the US Secretary of Education. Certification: Must hold current certification or recertification as a CRNA by the NBCRNA. Industry Awareness: Demonstrated knowledge of environmental and regulatory issues influencing nurse anesthesia practice and education. Perks & Professional Flexibility Tenure-Track Option: Faculty members have the option to pursue a tenure-track appointment. Clinical Practice Opportunity: Faculty in clinical programs have the unique opportunity to maintain active clinical practice by working up to 8 hours per week outside the University in their specialty. Why Join the University of Evansville? At the University of Evansville, our health sciences and graduate nursing programs are committed to rigorous education, interprofessional collaboration, and hands-on clinical excellence. You will join a supportive, mission-driven faculty dedicated to shaping the future of nurse anesthesia in a collaborative academic environment. How to Apply & Timeline Anticipated Start Date: January 1, 2027. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, media influences on mental and physical health; health communication and health behavior; social media and well-being; media representations of health, illness, and disability; stigma and stereotyping; cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to health-related media; health misinformation; and the development and evaluation of media-based interventions designed to improve health and well-being. Teaching opportunities may include courses in media psychology, strategic communications, health communication, social media, research methods, and other areas related to the candidate’s expertise.The primary criteria for this search are excellence in research and teaching related to media, behavior, and health. jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Psychology
jobs.description: Assistant Professor, Psychology Indianapolis, IN, United States (On-site) Be the First to Apply Job Description The Department of Psychology at Butler University (Indianapolis, IN) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Biological or Cognitive Psychology to start in August 2027. We seek a colleague who is committed to inclusive undergraduate teaching and collaborative research with undergraduate students. The Butler Psychology Department values candidates who share our commitment to engagement and inclusion of students, faculty, and staff with diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. Successful applicants will be broadly trained in psychology and will be ready to teach in a multidisciplinary university core curriculum. Standard teaching load is nine (9) credit hours per semester plus an active program of research involving undergraduate collaborators. We seek colleagues who will be ready to teach required psychology courses such as research methods and statistics (I & II) and introductory psychology. Additionally, the successful candidate will be able to teach at least one of the following: biological bases of behavior, cognitive processes, and/or learning, with the opportunity to teach upper-level electives in their related area of expertise. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to evidence-based and engaged-learning pedagogies and to building an inclusive classroom environment for an increasingly diverse student body. This position requires full-time, in-person instruction. A Ph.D. in Psychology or Cognitive/Behavioral Neuroscience (e.g., comparative psychology, computational neuroscience, or a related applied area such as health psychology) at the time of appointment is required. Applicants with an active research agenda in biological and/or cognitive areas will be prioritized. Applicants with research specializations that supplement and/or diversify the research expertise of our current faculty are especially encouraged to apply. The Butler University Psychology Department is housed in the Sally Beck Suite of the renovated Holcomb building and includes faculty offices, labs including a newly fitted EEG lab, vivarium to house rodents, and classrooms. More information about our department and the University can be found at: https://www.butler.edu/arts-sciences/psychology. Butler University offers support for faculty development in many ways, including start-up funds for research, internal grants for collaborative research with undergraduates, a learning community for new faculty, and funds for faculty and students to travel to present research. To apply, applicants should submit the following: Cover letter discussing qualifications for and interest in the position, including specific courses from our curriculum the candidate would be prepared to teachCV Teaching statement that includes evidence of effective, evidence-based, and inclusive teaching (e.g. sample syllabi, student evaluations, peer evaluations)Research statement that includes plans for a program of research involving undergraduate students transcripts of graduate work or other evidence of terminal degree(s) (unofficial is acceptable for candidate review) list of 3-5 references, including name, title, and contact information (shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide three letters of recommendation) The cover letter and CV can be uploaded individually. All other materials should be submitted as a single PDF. Review of applications will begin October 2nd, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Please direct questions to the search committee chair, Dr. Stacy Wetmore (swetmore@butler.edu). About Us Butler University is a private, nationally recognized comprehensive university encompassing seven colleges: Arts, Business, Communication, Education, Liberal Arts & Sciences, Pharmacy & Health Sciences and Founder's College. Approximately 4,500 undergraduate and 1,000 graduate and doctoral students

The successful applicant for this position will be able to demonstrate outstanding commitment to doctoral teaching and dissertation research mentorship.Any specialty area of interest/expertise in Clinical or Counseling Psychology is open. ABDs and doctoral candidates currently completing internship will be considered with the expectation of degree completion prior to starting the position. jobs.description: University of Notre Dame: College of Arts & Letters: Theology Location Notre Dame, IN Open Date Sep 11, 2026 Deadline Oct 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time Description The Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame in Notre Dame, Indiana, invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track professorship at the assistant professor rank in the field of Theology and Technology. The department is particularly interested in candidates who study the ethics of digital technologies. Successful candidates will demonstrate not only expertise in the applied ethics of technology but also grounding in broader theological sources. The starting date for this position will be August 23, 2027. Responsibilities will include research and publication, teaching and mentoring students at all levels—doctoral (and pre-doctoral), ministerial, and undergraduate—and service to the department and university. Information about Notre Dame is available at https://www.nd.edu/ , the Department of Theology at https://theology.nd.edu/ , and the University mission statement at https://www.nd.edu/about/mission/ . Qualifications The successful candidates will show evidence of strong scholarship and a trajectory toward a field-leading contribution to the study of theology and technology. They will also be sympathetic to the mission of the University of Notre Dame, which seeks a distinctive educational and scholarly excellence that is founded on its Catholic identity. Candidates at the entry level must have completed all requirements for a Ph.D. degree or have completed all but dissertation in moral theology or a closely related field with successful dissertation defense by August 1, 2027. Candidates at the advanced level must have a Ph.D. in moral theology or a closely related field. Application Instructions Please submit a letter of application, current curriculum vitae, one writing sample, and three letters of recommendation. Application Process This institution is using Interfolio's Faculty Search to conduct this search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials, including confidential letters of recommendation, free of charge. Apply Now Equal Employment Opportunity Statement The University of Notre Dame seeks to attract, develop, and retain the highest quality faculty, staff and administration. The University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or age in employment. Moreover, Notre Dame prohibits discrimination against veterans or disabled qualified individuals, and complies with 41 CFR 60-741.5(a) and 41 CFR 60-300.5(a). We strongly encourage applications from candidates attracted to a university with a Catholic identity. Dual Career Assistance To support relocating families, Notre Dame’s Dual Career Assistance Program helps spouses and partners pursue local career opportunities. Background Check This appointment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check. Applicants will be asked to identify all felony convictions and/or pending felony charges. Felony convictions do not automatically bar an individual from employment. Each case will be examined separately to determine the appropriateness of employment in the particular position. Failure to be forthcoming or dishonesty with respect to felony disclosures can result in the disqualification of a candidate. The full procedure can be viewed at https://facultyhandbook.nd.edu/?id=link-73597.

jobs.description: Assistant/Associate Professor - Civil Engineering (Transportation) Assistant/Associate Professor - Civil Engineering (Transportation) Full-time Angola, Indiana Summary The Reiners Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Trine University invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the rank of Assistant/Associate Professor with a preferred start date of August 2026. We seek a dynamic, student-centered educator who will contribute to our mission of promoting intellectual and personal development through professionally focused and formative learning opportunities. The successful candidate will demonstrate a passion for teaching, mentoring, and engaging undergraduate students in both classroom and laboratory settings while contributing to the continued growth of the civil engineering program. The faculty member will be expected to teach transportation engineering courses and support other areas of the curriculum based on departmental needs. The candidate will also pursue scholarly and professional activities that enhance undergraduate education and strengthen industry engagement. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Teaching and Mentoring Teach undergraduate civil engineering courses, including courses in transportation engineering. Teach courses in surveying, geographic information systems (GIS), and/or civil engineering materials. Support instruction in foundational civil engineering courses as needed. Develop engaging, hands-on learning experiences that emphasize conceptual understanding, problem-solving, and real-world applications. Supervise undergraduate design projects, including capstone design and experiential learning activities. Maintain regular office hours and provide thoughtful academic and career advising. Scholarship and Professional Development Engage in scholarly or professional activities consistent with the university’s mission and focused on enhancing undergraduate education. Involve undergraduate students in research, applied projects, or scholarly activities. Present scholarly work at conferences and/or publish in relevant journals or engineering education venues. Maintain professional engagement through participation in relevant professional societies and continuing professional development. Service Participate in departmental, college, and university service activities. Contribute to student recruitment, outreach, and industry engagement initiatives. Support ABET accreditation processes and continuous improvement efforts within the civil engineering program. Education and/or Experience Required Qualifications Ph.D. in Civil Engineering or a closely related field required Demonstrated commitment to undergraduate teaching and mentoring excellence. Effective communication skills and ability to work collegially in a collaborative academic environment. Preferred Qualifications Teaching experience at the undergraduate level (as instructor, lecturer, or TA). Experience or strong interest in active learning, project-based learning, and laboratory instruction. Record or potential for scholarly activity involving undergraduates (applied research, curriculum innovation, or engineering education). jobs.title: Byron K. Trippet Assistant Professor of History
jobs.description: The Wabash College History Department invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position in Medieval history to begin July 1, 2027, at the rank of Assistant Professor. A Ph.D. in History or a related field is required by the start date. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching and research in an undergraduate liberal arts setting. Teaching responsibilities consist of three courses per semester, including introductory world history courses, all-college courses, and advanced courses in non-Atlantic regional history, such as the Middle East, North Africa, or other related regions. The History Department at Wabash College currently offers courses in World, U.S., Latin American, and European history. This position is intended to extend the department’s coverage of medieval and non-Atlantic history while expanding the range of topics currently offered in advanced courses and seminars for majors and minors. Further information about the History Department is available at https://www.wabash.edu/academics/history. Wabash College offers competitive salaries and benefits with substantial support for professional travel and research as well as continued professional development orientations and workshops for all faculty. In the pre-tenure years, this position’s appointment is as a Byron K. Trippet professor, which provides additional teaching and research support. About Wabash College Founded in 1832, Wabash College is a private, independent, residential four-year liberal arts college with a mission to “educate men to think critically, act responsibly, lead effectively, and live humanely.” Its faculty is ranked No. 9 nationally for accessibility by the Princeton Review. The College invests significant resources to ensure students can participate in off-campus and international immersion learning experiences. Our 92-acre wooded campus is located in Crawfordsville, Indiana. Crawfordsville is a growing, vibrant community with easy access to outdoor recreation and facilities. Within 50 minutes of Indianapolis, Crawfordsville is close to an array of nationally recognized museums and sports facilities, including those housing the WNBA Fever, NBA Pacers, and NFL Colts. In the midst of a strategic transformation to advance the success of first-generation students and students from low-income families, Wabash College is committed to attracting and effectively supporting faculty and staff who are committed to student success. Approximately 25% of our students are federal Pell Grant recipients, one-third are first-generation college students, and about 20% identify as domestic students of color. Wabash offers a range of academic and cultural programs open to all members of the community. Wabash is a top-50 Liberal Arts College according to U.S. News and a member of Colleges That Change Lives. Many students, staff, and faculty find the close-knit community of the residential college one of the most rewarding aspects of joining the Wabash College community. Application Process To apply, go to www.wabash.edu/employment and click the “Apply Now” button. The application dossier should consist of: Letter of application Curriculum vita Teaching philosophy explaining how the candidate’s teaching and research would contribute to the department’s curriculum. Unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts Email addresses for three persons who will be asked to submit confidential letters of recommendation electronically Wabash College, a liberal arts college for men, seeks faculty and staff who are committed to providing quality engagement with students, high levels of academic challenge and support, and meaningful experiences that prepare students for life and leadership among diverse populations around the globe. Wabash is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from persons of all backgrounds.

You may also request a physical copy by emailing IU Public Safety at iups@iu.edu Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details Position Details Title Center for Possible Minds Postdoctoral Fellow Appointment Status Non-Tenure Track Department IU Bloomington Arts & Sciences; Dean Location Bloomington Position Summary Center for Possible Minds Postdoctoral Fellow Vacancy The Center for Possible Minds at Indiana University, Bloomington, invites applications for Postdoctoral Fellows to join its Program for Advanced Research in Diverse Intelligences. The fellowship provides support to scholars studying intelligence/cognition/mind in diverse forms, from diverse disciplinary perspectives. Candidates must embrace interdisciplinary scholarship and be excited about substantial conversation and collaboration with other disciplines. This postdoctoral fellowship program aims to create a cohort of researchers optimally positioned to address questions about the nature of biological, artificial, and collective intelligence through collaboration across a wide range of fields. We seek enthusiastic scientists and scholars who will embrace the chance to help set the agenda for our new research center. Postdoctoral fellows will have the opportunity to organize meetings and workshops at the Center as well as to propose new Center initiatives. We expect to hire 2-4 postdocs through this search. Postdocs will have offices in the Center for Possible Minds, where they will be joined by visiting fellows and faculty. Fellows are expected to pursue research activities associated with their primary area(s) of scholarship, as well as to explore collaborative, interdisciplinary projects. These fellowships are designed to advance the careers of new scholars by providing opportunities to research, organize, and collaborate in a highly interdisciplinary environment. Strong applicants will demonstrate evidence of the sort of outstanding scholarly potential that would make them competitive for tenure-track faculty positions at Indiana University or other top research universities. Terms of AgreementFellows are expected to pursue research, organize workshops and events, and participate in Center activities and seminars. Fellows may also teach classes in the appropriate department(s) or program(s), subject to curriculum needs and availability of funds. Fellowships are expected to be 2-year positions; fellows will be appointed as one-year contracts with the possibility for renewal. The start date is flexible; positions can begin as soon as August 1, 2026. Fellows will receive a salary of $60,000 plus health benefits and $3,000 each year in research support. Application ProcessWe invite applications from qualified candidates at the beginning of their academic careers who do not yet hold tenure-track academic positions. Applicants should submit the following materials: (1) a cover letter; (2) their CV; (3) a research statement describing their research and professional goals; (4) a one-page statement describing activities and initiatives they hope to organize through the Center; and (5) the names of 3 referees. Applications should be submitted online at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/32986. Cover letters should be addressed to: Professors Erica Cartmill and Jacob Foster, Center for Possible Minds, Indiana University, 815 10th St., Bloomington, IN 47405. Please send any questions to ericac@iu.edu and jacobf@iu.edu. Applications received by May 10, 2026 at 12:00 pm EST will receive full considerati

The appointment will be at the rank of full professor, beginning August 2027, and will be made in cooperation with the relevant disciplinary department. Candidates at the rank of associate professor would be considered in exceptional cases. Posting Details Position Details Title Director, Center for Constitutional Democracy and Professor of Law Appointment Status Tenure Department IU Bloomington Maurer School of Law Location Bloomington Position Summary The Indiana University Maurer School of Law is seeking an outstanding lateral candidate to join our faculty as a tenured professor of law and to serve in the role of Director of the Center for Constitutional Democracy. Founded in 2005, the Center has developed an impactful record of scholarship, teaching, international engagement, and practical assistance focused on constitutional democracy and the rule of law. Its work has included partnerships with scholars, lawyers, judges, public officials, and reformers confronting democratic transition, constitutional reform, institutional fragility, and threats to constitutional government. The Law School seeks a director who will build on this distinguished first chapter and help the Center envision the most important tools to understand and support democratic constitutional orders domestically and abroad in the years ahead. We welcome candidates whose interests connect constitutional democracy with fields such as law and political economy; comparative constitutionalism and democratic resilience; or technology, information systems, and democratic governance. These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive. The Center’s mission extends beyond any single domestic legal issue and calls for a director able to engage constitutional democracy across institutions, disciplines, and national boundaries. The director will oversee the Center’s programs and operations; work with affiliated faculty and students; develop conferences, lectures, and scholarly and applied projects; represent the Center to academic, professional, governmental, philanthropic, and international audiences; open professional opportunities for students, and teach courses related to its mission. Basic Qualifications Candidates should hold a J.D., Ph.D., or comparable terminal degree and possess a substantial record of scholarship and professional accomplishment, demonstrated leadership ability, and a strong commitment to constitutional democracy. jobs.title: Fellow for Student Success
jobs.description: Ivy Tech Community College Madison seeks a qualified and mission-driven full-time hourly staff member to serve as the Fellow for Student Success and Experience for our statewide Correctional Education program. This position is temporary in nature and will be reviewed annually for renewal. General Purpose/Position Summary: This position will support student success outcomes across Ivy Tech’s correctional education programs. Focus will be on strengthening the student experience, improving persistence and completion, supporting transitions between facilities and programs, and helping build future postsecondary pathways for students served in Indiana Department of Correction facilities. The Fellow will be based at the Ivy Tech Correctional Education Office in Plainfield, Indiana, and will work as part of the statewide Correctional Education team. This position will be embedded in the work of current programs while assisting with the planning, development, and implementation of future student success initiatives. This position is intended for an individual who brings strong student support skills, an understanding of barriers faced by justice-impacted learners through lived-experience, and a commitment to expanding educational opportunity. The Fellow will collaborate with correctional education leadership, faculty, staff, campus partners, and external stakeholders to identify student needs, strengthen communication and support systems, and contribute to measurable student success outcomes. The position may support projects related to student orientation, academic progress, student transfer between facilities, career pathways, re-entry preparation, student voice, transition to Ivy Tech campuses, and future college-credit programming. This role will help Ivy Tech think at a systems level about the student experience in correctional education. The Fellow will work across existing statewide functions, including assessment, special education and disability support, career and technical education, professional development, data, and regional facility support, to help identify gaps and recommend practical solutions. Major Responsibilities: -Support statewide student success initiatives within Ivy Tech Correctional Education. -Assist with tracking and improving student outcomes, including persistence, completion, transition, and progression into additional education or career pathways. -Work with correctional education staff to identify student barriers and recommend practical supports that improve the student experience. -Support existing high school equivalency, career and technical education, and college pathway programming across correctional facilities. -Assist with the design and development of future student success systems for expanded correctional education programs, including associate-level coursework. -Help strengthen the student experience for learners who transfer between facilities, complete programs, prepare for release, or seek to continue with Ivy Tech after incarceration. -Assist with coordination between Ivy Tech Correctional Education, facility-based education teams, HIRE, re-entry partners, and campus-based student support services. -Help gather student, faculty, and staff feedback to inform program improvement. -Support student-facing materials, orientations, communication tools, and transition resources. -Assist with projects related to career readiness, re-entry preparation, advising, student engagement, academic support, and future college-credit pathways. -Support planning for future associate-degree programs by helping identify what the student experience should look like before, during, and after enrollment. -Contribute to reports, presentations, meeting materials, and project updates related to correctional education student success. -Represent Ivy Tech professionally in meetings and partner conversations. -Maintain confidentiality and comply with Ivy Tech and Indiana Department of Correction policies and proc

jobs.description: Position Title: Instructor of Anthropology Compensation: 3000.00 per class Department: Department of Anthropology and Sociology - Temp Start Date: 01/11/2027 About this opportunity: The Department of Anthropology and Sociology invites applications for its temporary, part-time Instructor of Anthropology pool. Applicants selected for the pool may be offered assignments to teach one or two undergraduate courses per semester, depending on departmental instructional needs and course availability. These are temporary appointments and are not permanent or tenure-track positions. Candidates for searches must have current authorization to be employed in the U.S. without employer sponsorship. Applications will be held on file for one year. What you'll do and what you'll bring: Position Description: Faculty in the pool may be needed to teach a variety of undergraduate courses, such as Introduction to Cultural Anthropology, Archaeology and Culture, and Introduction to Biological Anthropology, in either online or in-person formats during the fall and spring semesters. Course assignments will vary based on departmental instructional needs and course availability. Minimum Qualifications: Master's degree in Anthropology from an accredited institution. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in Anthropology from an accredited institution and demonstrated excellence in teaching anthropology at the postsecondary level. Experience in teaching in-person and online classes. Area of specialization (as evidenced by coursework or teaching experience) congruent with departmental course needs. Commitment to high-quality teaching is essential. How to apply: Please provide the following: Required Documents: Cover Letter Curriculum Vitae Undergraduate Transcripts Optional Documents: Master's Transcripts If you have questions please contact: Robert Phillips rfphillips@bsu.edu 765-285-4845

jobs.description: Position Title: Instructor of English as Another Language Compensation: $1,600.00 - $2,000.00 Department: Div of Lifetime Learning, NonCredit - Temp Start Date: 08/31/2026 About this opportunity: We are seeking qualified, enthusiastic, and culturally competent candidates to join our Part-Time Adjunct Instructor Pool for Adult EAL (English as Another Language). We offer 8-week cohorts throughout the year, with our next session starting at the end of August. Applicants admitted to this pool will be reviewed and hired on an as-needed basis prior to the start of each cohort. Our in-person classes are taught at different locations: Fishers, Indianapolis, and Whitestown. We are currently seeking faculty for the Fishers location. This is a part-time temporary position teaching 32 hours total (2 hours, twice a week in the evenings) for 8 weeks. Continued teaching opportunities may be available. Salary will be based on experience. Candidates for searches must have current authorization to be employed in the U.S. without employer sponsorship. What you'll do and what you'll bring: Position Description: In this role, instructors facilitate dynamic, practical language instruction for adult learners aiming to improve their English for personal, professional, or academic goals. Position function and duties: Instruction: Deliver engaging, learner-centered English lessons focusing on speaking, listening, reading, and writing for real-world adult contexts. Lesson Preparation: Plan and adapt curriculum to meet the diverse needs, skill levels, and cultural backgrounds of adult students. Classroom Management: Foster a safe, supportive, and inclusive learning environment where adult students feel confident practicing new skills. Assessment & Tracking: Monitor student progress, provide constructive feedback, and maintain accurate attendance records. Communication: Coordinate with program administrators regarding curriculum, student needs, and facility logistics. Minimum qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree preferably in education, English, or TESOL Experience: Prior teaching experience Skills: Strong cross-cultural communication and interpersonal skills. jobs.description: Indiana Tech is a thriving, independent, teaching-oriented university that delivers career-oriented programming in a wide variety of disciplines that includes business, engineering, computer sciences, criminal justice, cybersecurity, marketing, health sciences, communication and helping professions. Indiana Tech enrolls nearly 1,500 students in its traditional undergraduate programs on its picturesque main campus, and nearly 5,000 students in its adult and online program. We offer degrees at the associate, bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral levels and undergraduate and graduate certificates. Over 41% of our students are either globally or domestically diverse; this contributes to our unique vibrant and inclusive campus community. All academic programs are designed to provide students with relevant and practical experiences, including an emphasis on internships. The university is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. Indiana Tech is committed to fostering a welcoming and respectful environment for all. We actively support the recruitment, engagement, and retention of students, faculty, and staff from a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We believe that creating a sense of connection and support across our campus community plays an essential role in preparing students to succeed and contribute in a global society. Indiana Tech has big plans for its future. Learn more at Indiana Tech Strategic Plan or strategicplan.indianatech.edu . Indiana Tech invites applications for a full-time faculty member in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Smart Manufacturing to join the Talwar College of Engineering and Computer Sciences. This 12-month teaching faculty position offers an exciting opportunity to educate and mentor students while contributing to the continued growth of innovative engineering and technology programs. The successful candidate will possess expertise in multiple areas of mechanics, thermofluids, advanced manufacturing, robotics and automation, smart manufacturing systems, and emerging physical AI technologies. Preference will be given to candidates who can teach across multiple disciplines, including mechanical engineering, industrial and manufacturing engineering, mechatronics and robotics engineering, and mechanical engineering technology. This position may be filled as either a tenure-track faculty appointment or at the Professor of Practice rank, depending on the qualifications, academic credentials, and professional experience of the selected candidate. Faculty members teach in both face-to-face and online formats and play a critical role in advancing engineering education through innovative teaching, curriculum development, and student engagement. Responsibilities include developing new academic programs, enhancing existing curricula, advising and mentoring students, supporting student recruitment and retention initiatives, collaborating with colleagues across disciplines, and contributing to continuous program improvement efforts. Faculty are also expected to maintain academic records to support accreditation activities, participate in ABET assessment and continuous improvement processes, utilize learning management systems and instructional technologies effectively, and support the mission, vision, and strategic priorities of Indiana Tech. Qualified candidates must possess a master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Manufacturing Engineering, or a closely related field, with a terminal degree preferred. Candidates with experience developing hands-on laboratory experiences, workforce training programs, or applied engineering curricula are especially encouraged to apply. Preference will be given to individuals with a demonstrated record of interdisciplinary collaboration across mechanics, engineering design, manufacturing systems, automation, or robotics. jobs.description: Job Title: Non-Credit Adjunct Instructor: Radioligand Therapy (RLT) Manufacturing & Operations Training Location: Indianapolis Job Type: Contracted Technical Training, Adjunct Instructor Classification: Skills Training Adjunct Faculty Salary Range: Salary varies - Based on qualifications and experience Reports To: Ivy+ Career Link Project Manager Who We Are: Ivy Tech is Indiana’s community college and workforce engine, delivering: high-quality learning experiences that propel Indiana’s communities, measurable economic return, excellence in teaching, and industry-aligned credentials of value, empowering every learner to achieve lifelong success Our Values: •Empathy - We lead with care and connectivity, ensuring we meet our students where they are. •Integrity - We act responsibly and ethically in the best interest of our students, employees, partners, institution, and the State. •Agility - We move with purpose and adapt to the evolving needs of our students, employers, and the State. •Impact - We exist to change lives through quality education. Our About The Role: The adjunct specialist for Radioligand Therapy is responsible for delivering a structured 32-hour foundational training program for incumbent employees and new operators entering radioligand therapy manufacturing operations. This role ensures learners achieve operator-level competency in radiopharmaceutical production, aseptic processing, radiation safety, and current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) requirements. The instructor will translate complex radiochemistry, sterile manufacturing principles, and regulatory expectations into applied, hands-on learning experiences that prepare employees to safely and effectively operate within a radioligand therapy production environment. They will also provide leadership on initiatives that strengthen the School’s visibility, impact and connections to practice in sustainability. The long-term teaching load for Clinical faculty is typically 6 courses per year, possibly with lighter starting loads and reductions to balance heavy service loads when those arise. Clinical faculty are not eligible for tenure but will be considered for promotion and/or long-term contracts no later than the sixth year of appointment. Salary and rank are commensurate with qualifications and experience. The expected start date is August 1, 2027. O’Neill-Bloomington contains a vibrant student and faculty community and is the largest school of public affairs and public policy in the United States, with over 4,000 students, and for five years has ranked in one of the top two spots of the U.S. News & World Report rankings for graduate public affairs schools in the country. Six of O’Neill’s specialty programs are ranked in the top five listings nationally; O’Neill is also tied for the top-ranked public administration program according to the 2020 Academic Ranking of World Universities. These are 10-month, non-tenure-track appointments with an 18-credit-hour annual teaching assignment.Professional Skills faculty teach primarily in Kelley Compass, a required three-course professional-development sequence for Kelley undergraduates. The sequence integrates career development with professional communication, leadership, teamwork, and professional identity development. Faculty typically have a primary assignment in one of the three Compass courses, with opportunities to teach across the sequence. Professional Skills Courses Compass 1: Professional Identity and Career Exploration (1.5 credits) Compass 1 introduces students to career development and professional identity. Students explore their values, interests, personality, and skills; investigate majors and career possibilities; learn to articulate their professional identity and value to professional audiences; and develop professional networking skills. Compass 2: Career Readiness and Job Search (1.5 credits) Compass 2 develops students’ career-readiness and recruiting skills. Course content includes employer research and career strategy, resumes, interviewing, professional correspondence and networking, giving and receiving actionable feedback, cultural competence, and emotional intelligence. Compass 3: Professional Communication, Leadership, and Teaming (1 credit) Compass 3 is the capstone of the required professional development sequence (this is an online, asynchronous course). The course emphasizes evidence-based professional communication, leadership, emotional intelligence, and effective participation in high-performance virtual teams. The Faculty RoleLecturers have both teaching and service obligations including curriculum development, pedagogical development and service to the Communication, Professional, and Computer Skills (CPCS) academic area, the Kelley School, Indiana University, and the broader community. Annual professional development funding is available for activities including conference travel, purchasing books, and research.These positions are based at the IUB campus in Bloomington, Indiana. jobs.description: University of Notre Dame: Mendoza College of Business: Information Technology, Analytics, and Operations Location Notre Dame, IN Open Date Sep 15, 2026 Deadline Nov 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time Description The IT, Analytics, and Operations (ITAO) Department, at the University of Notre Dame’s Mendoza College of Business, in collaboration with the Data, AI, and Computing Initiative (DAC), announces an open-rank position at the assistant, associate, or full professor level. The ideal candidate has a strong record of interesting and impactful scholarship or great potential for such scholarship. This entails significant publication success at premier outlets and/or a strong pipeline of innovative and rigorous research relevant to Data, AI, and Computing in business applications. Preference will be given to individuals whose research complements the interests of our existing faculty. Candidates pushing the envelope in exciting boundary-spanning areas at the intersection of business, analytical modeling, computational social science, machine learning, network science, human-centered artificial intelligence, or experimentation methods are encouraged to apply. The ITAO Department is home to a host of approaches and backgrounds, making for a vibrant research environment, which results in frequent, compelling, and unique collaborative research projects among our faculty. The department also houses the Human-centered Analytics Lab (HAL), Generative AI, Management, and Accountability Lab (GAMA), and the Humanitarian Operations Lab (HOPE). ITAO is well-aligned with the university's Data, AI, and Computing Initiative, which launched in September 2025. The initiative’s aim is to advance purposeful data, AI, and computing—excelling in foundational research while catalyzing interdisciplinary collaboration and real-world translation to address pressing societal challenges. Our ideal candidate will have demonstrated success in the classroom with an interest in teaching in areas related to analytics, broadly defined. In addition to our PhD program in Analytics, the ITAO Department offers an undergraduate major in Business Analytics, two AI minors, and a Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSBA) program. The Mendoza College of Business is home to a highly regarded Masters of Business Administration (MBA) program, for which we offer a major in Analytics & AI. The ITAO Department is an integral part of the University of Notre Dame’s interdisciplinary efforts to make an impact on scholarship and society through analytical modeling, operations research, data analytics, artificial intelligence, and computationally intensive research. There are also interdisciplinary collaborative opportunities, such as the possibility of affiliate faculty status in other departments (e.g., CS or Statistics) or the Lucy Family Institute for Data and Society. ITAO researchers enjoy generous allocations of resources from Notre Dame’s Center for Research Computing and the support of a staff of three full-time Mendoza College of Business data scientists and a director of behavioral research who oversees the Mendoza Behavioral Lab. Duties include research, teaching, and service. The teaching load is 9 credit hours per year and will also contribute to courses supporting our AI minors. Salary and research budget are highly competitive, with generous summer support based on research productivity. Successful candidates would, depending on qualifications and impact, be hired into a tenure-track assistant professor, tenured associate professor, or full professor role. Qualifications Candidates at the entry level must have completed all requirements for a Ph.D. degree or have completed all but dissertation in Analytics or a related field with degree expected by August 2027. Critical activities involve the synthesis of novel receptors. The intensive and extensive use of water in modern society places increasing demands on water supplies. This situation negatively impacts fresh water fit for human consumption and agricultural usage as well as the need in industry. Sustainable practices that either enable the removal of chloride from water or enable the performance of industrial processes even in chloride-laden waters are needed. Traditional approaches use reverse osmosis (RO) and electrodialysis across membranes, ion exchange with resin beads, or simple distillation. Despite advances in anion recognition chemistry, none of them use these principles, e.g., RO membranes leverage polyamide films that act as a size filter. This project seeks to take some of the first steps to leverage anion recognition chemistry for chloride sequestration and sensing in polymer materials. This postdoctoral scholar position involves the synthesis of new and known chloride-binding macrocycles and proof-of-concept testing of their ability to extract and sense chloride when incorporated into polymer materials. Responsibilities: 1. Organic synthesis of chloride-binding macrocycles, modify structures as needed to enable compatibility with polymer materials.2. Design and synthesize new chloride-binding macrocycles.3. Prepare polymer-based materials and characterize chloride extraction, and chloride capacity of polymer films.4. Proof-of-concept testing of turn-on fluorescent sensor for chloride using polymer materials and coatings5. Engage with industry and engineering collaborators.6. Fellows are expected to be in residence at the IU Indianapolis campus during the fellowship period, apart from research-related travel. They are envisioned to be equivalent to the tenure-track faculty position without requiring the responsibility of classroom teaching, or service and engagement, and without eligibility for tenure. Research Faculty are responsible for complying with all policies and procedures that relate to their employment and to their use of/access to university facilities and resources, both those now in effect and those adopted from time to time by the University. Colleges (including schools/departments and centers/institutes housed in colleges) that report to a dean and Discovery Park District (DPD) centers/institutes that report to the Executive Vice President for Research may employ Research Faculty in accordance with this policy. The Procedures for Research Faculty Appointment, Review and Promotion outline the requirements that must be met for Research Faculty to be appointed in these units. The primary responsibilities of Research Faculty are research and research-related activities, including but not limited to proposal writing, project supervision, and teaching/mentorship specifically linked to their scholarship and research programs (e.g., supervision of undergraduates, graduate students and Postdoctoral Researchers). Although Research Faculty do not have regular teaching duties, it is recognized that instances may occur when it is advantageous to expose students to a specialized expertise. In cases where a Research Faculty member is considered for a limited teaching assignment, a separate part-time teaching appointment is required. Such part-time teaching appointments must be prior approved by the Provost (West Lafayette) or Chancellor (Fort Wayne and Northwest). Appointments Research Faculty will be appointed with academic rank equivalent to tenure-track faculty (i.e., assistant professor, associate professor or full professor). The faculty rank of instructor is not available for Research Faculty. Qualifications for the three Research Faculty ranks are comparable to those of tenure-track ranks, but with primary or singular focus on research credentials. The ability to secure external funding does not automatically qualify individuals for Research Faculty appointments. Covey Professorship in Silk Road Studies. The successful candidate will contribute to the Department’s mission in the study of Central Eurasia and play a leading role in advancing Silk Road Studies across the Hamilton Lugar School and beyond.Applicants should have an established or emerging record of innovative research on the overland and/or maritime Silk Roads (2nd century BCE through 15th century CE) and their relevance to the contemporary world. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in one or more major languages necessary to conduct original research in their area of specialization, including the use of primary sources. Additionally, applicants should demonstrate excellence in teaching in Silk Road-related Studies, and a commitment to public engagement and program development of Silk Road Studies within the Department as well as within the Hamilton Lugar School. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to teach classes appealing to a broad range of students at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Teaching will be conducted in English. Review of applications will begin immediately, with all applications received by September 30, 2026 being guaranteed full consideration.The appointment begins August 1, 2027.Required Application Materials:Application materials must include a cover letter, curriculum vitae/resume, career statement describing research, service, teaching experiences and contact information of three academic referees, samples of published, in-press, and forthcoming research works, and previous teaching materials and course evaluations. jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty Position (Open Rank) - Robotics
jobs.description: University of Notre Dame: College of Engineering: Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering Location Notre Dame Main Campus Open Date Sep 03, 2026 Deadline Dec 01, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time Description The Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Notre Dame invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in robotics. This search is part of sustained growth in robotics at Notre Dame. Recent investments include the Physical AI and Robotics (PAIR) initiative, a cross-departmental effort that connects Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering with Computer Science and Engineering and with Electrical Engineering. Robotics at Notre Dame is organized around a distinctive identity in human-centered robotics, built on established strengths in mechanics, modeling, control, and experimentally grounded robotic systems. While applications are welcome from all areas of robotics, the Department is especially interested in candidates working in one or more of the following areas: ● Sensing, actuation, and robotic materials, including soft, multifunctional, and biohybrid systems ● Dexterous manipulation and physical interaction with complex or unstructured environments ● Wearable, assistive, and rehabilitation robotics, with particular interest in upper limbs ● Robotic mobility for terrestrial, aerial, and aquatic systems operating autonomously in extreme environments ● Integrated design, modeling, control, and estimation for emerging robotic systems Across these areas, the Department is particularly interested in candidates who advance robot learning and data-driven reasoning in ways that are grounded in the physics, mechanics, sensing, and control of real robotic systems and demonstrated through meaningful experimental deployment. The successful candidate will join an interconnected robotics community with active collaborations across engineering, computing, the health sciences, and industry, and with shared experimental facilities and testbeds that support work at the intersection of hardware, control, and learning. Additional information about robotics at Notre Dame is available at robotics.nd.edu. Qualifications The Department seeks to attract, develop, and retain exceptional faculty members with strong records of achievement and significant future potential. The search is primarily aimed at the assistant professor level; however, candidates at all ranks with strong records and promise will be considered, and possible position titles include Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor. Candidates at the entry level must have completed all requirements for a Ph.D. degree, or have completed all but the dissertation, in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a closely related field; candidates at the advanced assistant, associate, or full professor level must hold a Ph.D. in one of these fields. Duties for a successful candidate will include teaching, research and service. Successful candidates will demonstrate the potential to achieve an internationally distinguished record of scholarship, establish an externally funded research program, excel in undergraduate and graduate education, and contribute actively to their research community and to the University. Application Instructions Applicants are invited to provide any or all of the following: a cover letter; a curriculum vitae; a comprehensive research plan; a statement of teaching philosophy and interests; contact information for three professional references; and a statement regarding potential engagement with and commitment to the mission of the University of Notre Dame. All materials should be submitted via the application website. To guarantee full consideration, applications must be received by November 1, 2026; however, applications will be accepted until December 1, 2026.
